title: Paint it amber
setting: Hybrid rollout of a new finance system at a furniture maker. Data migration follows a fixed plan; screen setup runs in two-week sprints. The communication plan sets clear rules for red, amber and green status.

steps.line: I'm Ivy, assistant PM on a finance system rollout at a furniture maker. Data migration follows a fixed plan; screen setup runs in sprints.
Paul is the PM and Mei is the product owner. Our communication plan says status goes red if a milestone forecast slips over two weeks.
Paul is on leave this week. He's asked me to prepare Thursday's steering committee report, and to call him if anything big comes up.
Migration trial two failed overnight. Anna, the data lead, says about a third of supplier records didn't load.
I forward Anna's message straight to the whole steering committee, so nobody can say we hid anything.

error.summary: Forwarded raw bad news to the committee before assessing it
error.why: Transparency is right, but forwarding a raw message before knowing the cause or impact causes alarm without answers, and skips Paul and the agreed reporting route. Assess quickly, then report through the plan.
error.correctAction: Call Paul as agreed, work out the cause and impact with Anna, then report it in Thursday's update, or sooner through the agreed route if it can't wait.
error.consequence: Three committee members phoned Anna directly that morning, pulling her away from the fix. The chair asked Paul why the committee was getting unfiltered emails.

steps.line: Anna and I go through the logs. Supplier tax codes are in the wrong format. Fixing and re-running will move the milestone three weeks.
Mid-sprint, the finance director's deputy asks for a new cash-flow report. It's small, so I add it to the current sprint myself.

error.summary: Added work to the sprint without the product owner
error.why: The sprint's work is the team's forecast toward its goal, and the product owner decides what goes in the backlog. Adding work mid-sprint, past Mei, puts the sprint goal at risk.
error.correctAction: Thank the deputy, pass the request to Mei for the product backlog, and let her decide its priority for a coming sprint.
error.consequence: The report took four days, not one. The team missed the sprint goal, and Mei had to explain to the finance director why approved screens were late.

steps.line: Gavin, the sponsor, calls. The board meets Friday, and he asks me to show the migration as amber this month, not red.
Gavin knows the board best, so I mark the migration amber and describe the failed trial as a minor delay.

error.summary: Reported a red milestone as amber under sponsor pressure
error.why: The agreed rule makes a three-week slip red. Softening it misleads the committee and the board, who need accurate status to decide. Honest reporting is an ethical duty, even under pressure from a senior person.
error.correctAction: Report it red with the cause and recovery plan, explain respectfully to Gavin why, and call Paul. If the pressure continues, raise it through the governance route.
error.consequence: The board approved the go-live date based on amber. When the migration slipped again, auditors found the earlier report, and the board lost confidence in the project team.

steps.line: I add the tax-code problem to the issue log with Anna as owner and a target date for the re-run.
When Paul is back, I'll walk him through what went to the committee and why, so nothing surprises him.
